Other links: 1 : 0..N
Developer and Job: M : N via Application

Read a link as parent to child. Each child has exactly one parent. User to either profile is optional one-to-one. All remaining links are one-to-zero-or-many. Applications resolve the developer-to-job many-to-many relationship. Status history is the SQL audit extension.

users
id PK, name, email UK, password_hash, role, created_at

developer_profiles
id PK, user_id FK/UK, bio, phone, location, education, experience, github_url, linkedin_url, resume_path

recruiter_profiles
id PK, user_id FK/UK, company_name, company_description, location, website

skills
id PK, developer_id FK, name, level, years
UK (developer_id, name)

projects
id PK, developer_id FK, name, description, github_link, project_link

project_technologies
id PK, project_id FK, name, category, version, added_at
UK (project_id, name)
FK links: profiles.user_id = users.id; skills/projects.developer_id = developer_profiles.id; technologies.project_id = projects.id

PK means primary key. FK means foreign key. UK means uniqueness. The schema labels include all model attributes, not only a selected subset. Resume analysis text fields store narrative/extraction results, while searchable skills use separate rows.

application_status_history (SQL audit extension)
id PK, application_id FK, old_status, new_status, changed_at
FK parents: jobs / recruiter_profiles; job_skills / jobs; applications / developers and jobs; analysis / developers; history / applications

The first four entities are application models. application_status_history is installed by mysql_demo.sql. Each table has a primary key and at least five attributes. All child foreign keys refer to the parent id.

1NF: one skill or technology per child row
job_skills and project_technologies replace comma-separated operational lists.
2NF: facts depend on the complete key
Skill level and years describe a developer-skill pair. Application status describes a developer-job application.
User credentials, company details and job details stay in their own tables. Applications reference developers and jobs through foreign keys.

The normalized operational skill and technology records use one row per value. Narrative resume-analysis text is distinct from the normalized searchable skills. Key facts belong to their entity. The score is calculated, not duplicated in applications.

SELECT u.name, s.name AS skill, s.level
FROM users u
JOIN developer_profiles d ON d.user_id = u.id
JOIN skills s ON s.developer_id = d.id
WHERE s.name LIKE '%Python%'
ORDER BY u.name;

SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS total
FROM applications
GROUP BY status ORDER BY total DESC;
Search candidate skills and summarize application decisions with relational queries.

First query joins users, developer profiles and skills, filters Python with LIKE and sorts names. Second query groups application statuses. Results depend on the current database.

DELIMITER $$
CREATE TRIGGER log_application_status
AFTER UPDATE ON applications FOR EACH ROW
BEGIN
  IF OLD.status <> NEW.status THEN
    INSERT INTO application_status_history
      (application_id, old_status, new_status)
    VALUES (NEW.id, OLD.status, NEW.status);
  END IF;
END$$
DELIMITER ;
A saved status change creates an audit row with the old status, new status and time.

Match (%) = matched required skills ÷ total required skills × 100
Above 70%: Shortlisted. Recruiters can change the initial status after review.

ats_match normalizes required skills and the union of profile plus latest extracted resume skills. Match is the percentage of required names present. New scores above 70 are Shortlisted, and scores at or below 70 are Rejected. Recruiters can override these initial statuses. This does not evaluate experience, skill depth or overall competence.
